method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file, which was edited after r2: title and title.canDo, spec.situation and spec.deviation.reason, story beat and cliffhanger, the Folge (8 lines and the gist item), the three inputs (30 lines, the practice sign with its new afternoon hours, and the booking confirmation), the 9 exam texts, 2 strategy cards, 8 redemittel, the Sp2 task (instructions, situation, cards, aiRole, openingLine, 8 hintWords, 8 model turns), the S2 task (title, situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte, checklist, model text), the 2 check lines, every endLine, promptDe, option, hint and explanation.de, both rule cards (prose and tables), and the u07 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json with their examples. We solved all 93 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line (1 gist, 15 input, 12 structured, 33 pool, 13 reserve, 9 exam, 8 check, 2 proof), and the 8 perception items. We permuted every sentence_building item against its frame. For each of the 8 error corrections we listed every correct correction. We ran 33 candidate answers through the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js, and re-graded all 147 accepted forms of the 101 items: all are correct. We checked the exam blocks against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json: l3 has 5 × richtig_falsch on signs with location, 10–25 words; h3 is abc with 2 plays, reduced and scaffolded as a1.1 allows; sp2 is cards-ask with 2 topics; s2 has 3 Leitpunkte and about 30 words. We recomputed the word counts with lib-validate/text.mjs: signs 15/20/16/17/18, messages 36/31/37/33. We walked the lexical surface with a script built on lib-validate/lexicon.mjs (knownForms and licensedForms at a1.1-u07, compounds, the metalanguage allowlist). It covered every string of the unit, including hints, model turns and the rule cards. A second pass listed the always-known core and function words that some lexicon allocates to a later unit. We tested the r2-F01 gate by validating a scratch copy of the unit (in the session scratchpad, not in the repo) with ls2-p10 and ls3-r04 put back to their r2 state. We checked the cast against casts/a1.json and series.json, and the story against u05, u06, u08 and a1.2-u04. We checked the new practice hours against a1.2/lexicon.json lx.praxis and against the specs that reuse cast.dr-sommer (a1.2 u05, a2.1, b1.1). We checked the rule cards against rc.ja-nein-frage and against u08 and u11. We read ItemView.jsx (hint and maskQuote) and strings.js ltext for how a hint is shown: only hint.main, in the UI language. We read the rail code the findings depend on: ITM-01, ITM-09, LEX-01, LEX-03, core-lexicon.mjs, text.mjs FUNCTION_WORDS and metalanguage.mjs walkReadSurfaces. Every German replacement proposed below was run through the same knownForms walk, TXT-04 and the word counter.

On the sign, German practices usually write „vormittags“ for 8–12. lx.vormittag is not taught until u11, so „am Morgen“ is the defensible choice at u07, provided F02 stops defining it as seven or eight o'clock.

findings.problem: There are two problems on the one item that teaches the morgen/Morgen contrast. (1) The distractors are not the idiomatic forms. In Germany the fixed pairs are „heute Morgen“ and „heute Abend“; „heute am Abend“ is marked (Austrian, or emphatic). The unit itself says „heute Abend“ in the Folge and in the cliffhanger, and u11 uses „heute Morgen“ as an option. The explanation's rule „„morgen“ ohne „am“ ist der nächste Tag“ then fails on „heute Morgen“, which the learner meets four units later. (2) The explanation defines „am Morgen“ as „um sieben oder acht Uhr“. In the same Lernschritt, the sign, Arjun's lines, ls2-i02's explanation and ls2-i03 („Am Morgen offen bis ___ Uhr“ → 12) use „am Morgen“ for the whole forenoon, up to 12 Uhr. The learner gets two definitions of the word in one step. The key is not wrong, and the item still has exactly one right answer.
findings.fix: Options „heute Morgen“ / „am nächsten Tag“ / „heute Abend“; the key is unchanged. explanation.de: „„morgen“ (klein) ist der nächste Tag. „Morgen“ (groß) ist eine Tageszeit: am Morgen, heute Morgen.“ This is 15 words, all known at a1.1-u07, and the quoted sentence in the prompt shows the lower-case „morgen“. explanation.en to match („morgen“ in lower case = tomorrow; „Morgen“ with a capital = morning: am Morgen, heute Morgen). findings.problem: r2-F05 is unchanged. The unit drills, builds and elicits aufmachen and zumachen, the verbs of its Öffnungszeiten can-do, but no lexicon of the eight levels allocates them. So they reach no vocabulary card, no review ladder and no LEX-02 count, and A1.2 cannot know they were taught. We can now say why no rule reports it, which corrects r2's reading. The validator's core list carries both verbs as always-known A1 lemmas, and knownForms() skips a core lemma only when a lexicon allocates it to a later unit. With no allocation at all, the core makes „macht … auf“ known from u01 on. LEX-03's bracket check looks „(aufmachen)“ up in the lexicon and silently skips a cue that no lexicon has. So LEX-03 does not pass these items by splitting machen + auf.
findings.fix: Lexicon owner, as r2-F05 asked: add lx.aufmachen and lx.zumachen at a1.1-u07, productive, and let spec.lexiconBlocks follow (LEX-05). Bring the unit back to ≤ 35 new words together with F05, for example by making lx.anrufbeantworter and lx.geoeffnet gloss-only. No unit edit.
